question: The title "Zinda Pir" or "Living Saint" was attributed to:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Aurangzeb**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The title "Zinda Pir" or "Living Saint"** was attributed to **Aurangzeb**, the sixth Mughal emperor of India.
 
• Aurangzeb was known for his **piety and strict adherence to Islamic principles**, which earned him this title.
 
• He was highly devout and carried out his religious duties with dedication, which included performing regular prayers and fasting.
 
• Aurangzeb was also known for his personal simplicity and ascetic lifestyle, avoiding indulgence in the luxurious lifestyle often associated with Mughal emperors.
 
• His commitment to religion and moral conduct led his followers to regard him as a saintly figure, thereby calling him "Zinda Pir."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Aurangzeb:**

 
 
• Born on **3 November 1618**, Aurangzeb was the son of Shah Jahan and Mumtaz Mahal.
 
• He ruled from **1658 to 1707**, making him the longest-reigning Mughal emperor.
 
• He expanded the Mughal Empire to its greatest territorial extent, covering almost the entire Indian subcontinent.
 
• Aurangzeb is remembered for his **religious orthodoxy** and implementation of Islamic laws, such as the reimposition of the Jizya tax on non-Muslims.
 
• Despite his religious fervor, his policies were controversial, leading to dissent among certain communities and regions.
 
 
 
• **Other Mughal Emperors:**
 
 
• **Akbar:** Known as "Akbar the Great," he ruled from **1556 to 1605**. Akbar was famous for his policy of religious tolerance and his efforts to integrate diverse cultures within the empire.
 
• **Babur:** The founder of the Mughal Empire, Babur ruled from **1526 to 1530**. He was known for his military conquests and establishing Mughal rule in India.
 
• **Jahangir:** Jahangir ruled from **1605 to 1627**. He was known for his love for art, nature, and his administrative reforms.
 
 
 
• **Religious Policies of Aurangzeb:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb's reign was marked by his strict adherence to Islamic principles, including the enforcement of Sharia law.
 
• He banned practices that he deemed un-Islamic, such as music and certain festivals, which led to criticism from various sections of society.
 
• Despite his policies, he maintained a vast and efficient administrative system that contributed to the empire's prosperity.
 
 
 
• **Legacy:**
 
 
• Aurangzeb's legacy remains a subject of debate among historians due to his religious orthodoxy and administrative policies.
 
• While he expanded the empire and maintained strict governance, his policies alienated certain communities, leading to resistance and eventual weakening of the Mughal Empire after his death in **1707**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Aurangzeb's title "Zinda Pir"** is indicative of his personal religious devotion rather than his political or administrative achievements.
 
• His reign saw significant military expansion but also laid the groundwork for the eventual decline of the Mughal Empire due to his rigid policies.
 
• Despite controversies, Aurangzeb's ascetic lifestyle and devout practices left a lasting impression on the cultural and religious history of India.
